For rows i=0,1,2, the figure places A_i=D Psi_i(s_i) in column i and -I_d in column i+1. Its other six interior entries are zero. These are exactly the derivatives computed locally in proof step 1.1; the minus sign follows from subtracting the independent next segment start.

At N=3, F_3=B(s_0,s_3) has derivative D_1B in column 0 and D_2B in column 3, with zero columns 1 and 2, exactly as proof step 1.2 computes. The label definitions B_0 and B_3 in Remarks fix evaluation at (s_0,s_3). No equality of these two blocks is asserted.

The figure is explicitly an N=3 illustration of the general N>=1 statement. Eight outlines indicate potentially nonzero blocks; the accompanying prose warns they need not actually be nonzero. It asserts neither invertibility nor existence of a BVP solution. The original rigorous proof is unchanged and independent of the figure.
